LESSON MENU
Digital to analog conversion changes digital signals to analog signals.
DISCUSSION
D/A converter circuits accept binary inputs to generate analog voltages.
Recall that each binary column value is twice the value of the preceding column value.
A D/A converter circuit generates voltages to represent the binary column values.
There are two methods to accomplish the conversion. Let's look at weighted D/A conversion first.
A network of four resistors represents a binary number with four digits. One resistor is required for each input.
Each binary digit's value is represented by a resistor value.

The weighted D/A converter places a 0 volt potential at TP1 using an op-amp.
When a high is applied to input D, current flows through resistor R.
The source of the current is from the output of the op-amp through Rout.
The current path is between input D and the op-amp output through Rout.
The source of the current is from the output of the op-amp through Rout.Y
Current does not flow from the inverting input (-) of the op-amp due to the very high input impedance.
Current does not flow thru the inverting input (-) of the op-amp due to the very high input impedance.
The current flow produced by R develops a voltage across Rout. This is the analog output voltage.
The amount of voltage depends on the current generated by resistor R.
Resistor R has the lowest resistance. Voltage produced by the high input of D generates the largest voltage output.
Resistor 2R has the second lowest resistance and generates half as much voltage as resistor R.
Resistor 4R generates half as much voltage as 2R and resistor 8R generates half as much voltage as 4R.
When more than one input is high, the currents combine. Four inputs are available and 16 different outputs are possible.
For example in this circuit, a high on input D and C produces 3 volts.

The other method of D/A conversion uses scaling resistors. They divide the input into fractional values.
With four binary inputs there are 16 combinations possible.
CALCULATING BINARY COMBINATIONS - Since there are two possible outputs for every binary input, multiply the number 2 by the n power (n being the number of inputs).
With four binary inputs there are 16 combinations possible.
The circuit divides +5 volts into 16 equal parts, then combines the parts to produce 16 different output voltages.
The smallest voltage generated is 1/16 of the input voltage. This is called the resolution voltage.

RESOLUTION - Resolution voltage is the smallest increment of voltage that can be expressed. It is essentially the voltage represented by the LSD in the binary input, therefore: resolution is a function of the number of bits.
The smallest voltage generated is 1/16 of the input voltage. This is called the resolution voltage.
